channel.title: The Grant Desk - Grants, Media Arts, Film & Sound, UK, weekly digest
channel.description: Paid open calls, fellowships and residencies in AI, tech, research, and digital and mixed-media arts, sorted into the right pile. Updated as new calls land on the desk. Filtered to: Grants, Media Arts, Film & Sound, UK, weekly digest. Released weekly: each Sunday's drop carries one entry per grant added in the week before it (Sunday to Saturday). A call that closes before its drop goes out is not sent; the website lists those.

item.title: Arts Council of Northern Ireland: Individual Artists Digital Evolution Awards 2026/27 (up to GBP 10,000 for digital art) (closes 26 Nov)
item.description:
Arts Council of Northern Ireland (National Lottery funded)
Deadline: 26 Nov 2026, 12:00 GMT
Award: Up to GBP 10,000 per award. The applicant's own artist fees can be budgeted at up to GBP 125 a day or GBP 500 a week. No application fee stated.

A National Lottery award from the Arts Council of Northern Ireland for individual artists to make digital art and build skills in new media and immersive practice.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Hackney Showroom NICE PAIR 2027: commission for four double acts at the Lyric Hammersmith Studio (GBP 3,000 per artist) (closes 29 Nov)
item.description:
Hackney Showroom, in residence at the Lyric Hammersmith Theatre (supported by Arts Council England)
Deadline: 29 Nov 2026, 17:00 GMT
Award: GBP 3,000 per individual artist (GBP 6,000 per pair) for four weeks of work. Travel covered and accommodation with hosts provided for artists not based in London. No application fee mentioned.

Hackney Showroom is commissioning four double acts to make brand-new shows for NICE PAIR, a two-week festival of double acts in the Lyric Hammersmith's Studio in March 2027.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Tamasha SHIFT Artist Labs 2027: six-month funded development for new live performance (GBP 7,000 per project) (closes 30 Nov)
item.description:
Tamasha Theatre Company, with BEZNA Theatre, Roots Mbili, Beyond Face and HighTide
Deadline: 30 Nov 2026, 23:59 GMT
Award: GBP 7,000 research and development funding per project (five projects). Travel to the in-person days, and accommodation for the final two days, covered for artists based outside London. No application fee mentioned.

Tamasha funds five projects through a six-month development lab for artists with bold new ideas that respond to the world we live in now. Each project is matched with a dramaturg (Dannielle Rhimes Lecointe or Justine Themen), a Tamasha producer and an industry steward from a partner company.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: n-Space Fellowship, Singapore Fellow (Prediction): 9-month art and technology fellowship with 3 months at Somerset House Studios, London (GBP 5,000 fee, travel and accommodation covered) (closes 7 Dec)
item.description:
Somerset House Studios with the National Arts Council Singapore; research partner UAL Creative Computing Institute; supported by the Rothschild Foundation
Deadline: 7 Dec 2026, 10:00 GMT
Award: GBP 5,000 fellowship fee, plus return flights to London, accommodation, per diems and ground transport for both London visits, and access to a GBP 30,000 R&D fund shared by the six-person cohort. No application fee mentioned.

The Singapore place in the second n-Space fellowship cohort at Somerset House Studios, run with the National Arts Council Singapore.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: n-Space Fellowship, second cohort (Prediction): 18-month research fellowship at Somerset House Studios, London (GBP 10,000 fee plus shared GBP 30,000 R&D fund) (closes 7 Dec)
item.description:
Somerset House Studios, with UAL Creative Computing Institute, Abandon Normal Devices, Lancaster University and the National Arts Council Singapore; supported by the Rothschild Foundation
Deadline: 7 Dec 2026, 10:00 GMT
Award: London track: GBP 10,000 fee and access to a GBP 30,000 shared R&D fund, with 24/7 workspace. No travel, relocation or accommodation support. Singapore track: GBP 5,000 fee plus return flights, accommodation, per diems and ground transport, and the same shared fund. Up to GBP 200 towards an access support worker for the application. No application fee mentioned.

n-Space at Somerset House Studios is a space for experimental, collaborative research across art, technology and society, aimed at outcomes that do not fit traditional institutional platforms. Its second fellowship cohort is convened around PREDICTION.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: University of Exeter Arts and Culture: Arts Commission 2026/27 (organisational cultures and narrative infrastructure) (closes 29 Nov)
item.description:
University of Exeter Arts and Culture, with the Faculty of Humanities, Arts and Social Sciences (HASS)
Deadline: 29 Nov 2026
Award: Artist fee GBP 14,000 (incl. VAT, also covering travel, subsistence and accommodation) plus a production and presentation budget of up to GBP 4,000; a freelance creative producer is paid separately. Interviewed candidates receive GBP 100. No application fee.

The University of Exeter's annual flagship Arts Commission invites a creative practitioner in any artform interested in organisational cultures (how people work together in formal settings, and how those cultures can be disrupted, adjusted and reimagined) to work with academics in the Faculty of...

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Film London FLAMIN Productions 2026 (GBP 40,000 artists' moving-image commission) (closes 9 Dec)
item.description:
Film London (FLAMIN)
Deadline: 9 Dec 2026, 12:00 GMT
Award: GBP 40,000 production funding including artist fee; longlisted artists paid GBP 200, the final 2 to 3 paid GBP 1,000 to develop full proposals.

FLAMIN Productions funds one ambitious artists' moving-image work. ELIGIBILITY: artist filmmakers with a main address in England, at least five years of professional practice and a track record of exhibitions or festivals; no students; XR, games and genre projects are excluded.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Spike Island Open Call 2028: South West-Based Artist Commission (GBP 4,000 fee + GBP 8,500 production) (closes 13 Dec)
item.description:
Spike Island
Deadline: 13 Dec 2026, 23:59 GMT
Award: GBP 4,000 artist fee plus GBP 8,500 production budget; travel, accommodation and per diems covered.

A major gallery commission at Spike Island in Bristol, in any medium, culminating in an exhibition in summer 2028. ELIGIBILITY: artists who live and have their main studio in South West England; current undergraduates are excluded.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Southwark Charities: Public Art Commission, 220 Blackfriars Road (London garden commission) (closes 4 Jan 2027)
item.description:
Southwark Charities
Deadline: 4 Jan 2027
Award: Budget of about GBP 200,000 to 300,000 covering all costs (per ArtRabbit; the official page does not state a figure); up to 5 shortlisted artists are paid.

A public art commission for a 12 x 12 metre public garden beside a new affordable almshouse opening in early 2029. The brief is open on form, including lighting, text and paving. ELIGIBILITY: artists, designers and interdisciplinary teams at any career stage; Southwark connections welcomed.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Royal Society of Sculptors: First Plinth Public Art Award 2027 (GBP 20,000 commission) (closes 12 Jan 2027)
item.description:
Royal Society of Sculptors
Deadline: 12 Jan 2027
Award: GBP 20,000 commission for the winner; up to 5 shortlisted artists receive GBP 1,000 each for maquettes. Entry fee about GBP 34 (GBP 17 early bird until 17 November).

The First Plinth award commissions a large-scale sculpture for the plinth outside the Royal Society of Sculptors' Dora House in London, later moving to a second site. ELIGIBILITY: any artist working in three dimensions.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: The Whickers Film & TV Funding Award 2027 (GBP 120,000 for a first feature documentary) (closes 22 Jan 2027)
item.description:
The Whickers
Deadline: 22 Jan 2027, 12:00 GMT
Award: GBP 120,000 main award; GBP 25,000 development award for the runner-up. Free to enter.

The Whickers Film & TV Funding Award backs a director-led documentary by a first-time feature director. The winner receives GBP 120,000 and the runner-up a GBP 25,000 development award.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Screen South Showcase Artists 2026-27, Round 2 (digital creative bursaries up to GBP 1,500) (closes 29 Jan 2027)
item.description:
Screen South
Deadline: 29 Jan 2027
Award: Bursaries up to GBP 1,500 plus possible exhibition space.

Screen South supports digital creative projects (visual, immersive and sound-based) that are already underway and can be shown within six months; linear film is unlikely to be funded. ELIGIBILITY: artists based in South East England, excluding London.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Cultural Bridge 2027-28, Round 6: UK-Germany partnerships in social and community arts (up to GBP 30,000) (closes 10 Feb 2027)
item.description:
Cultural Bridge (British Council, Goethe-Institut, Fonds Soziokultur and the four UK arts councils)
Deadline: 10 Feb 2027, 12:00 GMT
Award: Up to GBP 30,000 per partnership plus access costs, from a GBP 360,000 pot (about 12 awards). No application fee.

Cultural Bridge funds partnerships between UK and German arts organisations working in social and community arts practice. Round 6 is limited to established (Tier 2) partnerships with a track record of working together.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Iris Prize 2027: International LGBTQ+ Short Film Prize (GBP 40,000) (closes 2 Jun 2027)
item.description:
Iris Prize
Deadline: 2 Jun 2027
Award: GBP 40,000 for the winner to make their next short film in the UK; smaller UK-only awards (Community and Education GBP 250, Micro Short GBP 100). Submission fee not stated on the official page; Iris alumni get a full waiver.

Billed as the world's largest LGBTQ+ short film prize, the Iris Prize international shorts strand is open worldwide; the Best British, student, community and education strands are UK only. Submissions open 11 January 2027; deadlines: early bird 31 March, regular 24 May, late 2 June 2027.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Awesome Foundation Local Chapters: USD 1,000 Monthly Micro-grants (US, UK, Canada, Australia, NL, Asia) (rolling)
item.description:
Awesome Foundation (local chapters)
Deadline: Rolling, apply any time
Award: Usually USD 1,000 (or local equivalent) per grant, no strings attached, typically one grant per chapter per month. No application fee.

The Awesome Foundation is a network of volunteer giving circles: in each chapter about ten trustees pool their own money to give a USD 1,000 no-strings micro-grant, usually monthly, to a project that adds "awesome" to their area: art, public interventions, community tech, events, science and civic...

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Studio Voltaire: Tender Living Residency 2027 (trans and non-binary artists; GBP 300/week for 10 weeks) (closes 22 Nov)
item.description:
Studio Voltaire
Deadline: 22 Nov 2026, 23:59 GMT
Award: GBP 300 per week for 10 weeks (GBP 3,000), plus mentoring and access funds.

A ten-week live/work residency at Studio Voltaire in London for emerging trans, non-binary or gender-questioning visual artists. ELIGIBILITY: emerging artists based in the UK outside London. OFFER: GBP 300 per week for 10 weeks, a live/work studio, mentoring and access funds.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: National Festival of Making: Art in Manufacturing Open Call 2027 (GBP 8,000 factory residencies) (closes 23 Nov)
item.description:
National Festival of Making
Deadline: 23 Nov 2026, 12:00 GMT
Award: GBP 8,000 commission per residency plus up to GBP 600 travel and accommodation.

Two paid residencies inside working factories (Crown Paints and Fox's Burton's Companies), with the resulting work shown at the National Festival of Making in Blackburn in late June 2027. ELIGIBILITY: artists and makers, individuals or collectives, based in the UK or Ireland.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Freelands Foundation: Two Together, Porthmeor Studios Residencies 2027 (GBP 2,000 per artist) (closes 30 Nov)
item.description:
Freelands Foundation
Deadline: 30 Nov 2026, 10:00 GMT
Award: GBP 2,000 per artist plus travel; shared studio and accommodation.

Two Together pairs two artists who share Studio 5 at Porthmeor Studios in St Ives and shared accommodation for a month. ELIGIBILITY: joint applications from two UK-based studio artists with five or more years of practice, one based in Devon or Cornwall, who are not an existing duo.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: BFI NETWORK England: Early Development Fund (GBP 3,000-5,000 treatment awards for debut long-form writers) (closes 11 Nov)
item.description:
BFI NETWORK (BFI, National Lottery funding)
Deadline: 11 Nov 2026
Award: GBP 3,000 to 5,000 per project to develop a treatment (stage one). Projects completed to schedule can then apply for second-stage funding to write a full first draft. National Lottery funding; no application fee stated.

BFI NETWORK's Early Development Fund supports writers at the very start of a debut long-form project: those who do not yet have a first draft of a script (or the equivalent format for immersive work).

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Connected Canvas: The National Gallery Digital Commission 2027 (emerging UK creatives) (closes 17 Nov)
item.description:
National Gallery (National Gallery X), London
Deadline: 17 Nov 2026, 23:59 GMT
Award: GBP 15,000 commission. Up to 10 shortlisted applicants receive GBP 500 each to develop proposals.

National Gallery X commissions a new digital, generative, screen-based or sound work for its three-screen LED canvas in the gallery. Open to UK-based emerging creatives in their first five years of practice who are not in full-time education.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Youth Music: Trailblazer Fund (Round 14) (closes 20 Nov)
item.description:
Youth Music
Deadline: 20 Nov 2026, 17:00 GMT
Award: GBP 2,000 to GBP 30,000 for organisations in England. No application fee.

Youth Music's Trailblazer Fund gives GBP 2,000 to GBP 30,000 to organisations in England running projects that let children and young people aged 25 or under make, learn and earn in music.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Refugee Festival Scotland 2027 x Opening Shot: Open Call for First-Time Filmmakers (GBP 1,500 fee plus GBP 3,000 production budget) (closes 22 Nov)
item.description:
Refugee Festival Scotland (Scottish Refugee Council) with Opening Shot
Deadline: 22 Nov 2026
Award: GBP 1,500 participation fee plus a GBP 3,000 production budget per filmmaker, with mentoring and a premiere screening at Refugee Festival Scotland in June 2027. Four filmmakers selected. No application fee stated.

Refugee Festival Scotland (run by the Scottish Refugee Council, festival 11 to 20 June 2027) and Opening Shot invite four first-time filmmakers with lived experience of seeking safety to make a short film of about five minutes.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Youth Music: Recharge Fund, Racial Equity (up to GBP 120,000 core funding over four years) (closes 4 Dec)
item.description:
Youth Music
Deadline: 4 Dec 2026, 17:00 GMT
Award: Core funding of up to GBP 120,000 over four years per organisation, from a total pot of GBP 2,400,000. No application fee.

Youth Music's Recharge Fund: Racial Equity gives multi-year core funding to creative organisations across England that are led by communities who experience racial injustice and that work with children and/or young people of different ages and backgrounds.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Creative Debuts: Black Artists Grant (BAG), GBP 500 monthly no-strings grant for UK-based Black artists (rolling)
item.description:
Creative Debuts
Deadline: Rolling, apply any time
Award: GBP 500 per recipient, one recipient per month. Unrestricted, no outcomes or reporting required. No application fee.

The Black Artists Grant (BAG) is a no-strings-attached monthly grant run and sponsored by Creative Debuts, the London-based platform for emerging artists.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: BRAID Creative Commissions 2027: A Promise in Return (Responsible AI, GBP 8,000-12,000, Edinburgh Art Festival)
item.description: BRAID (Bridging Responsible AI Divides), University of Edinburgh, with Inspace, the Institute for Design Informatics and the Edinburgh Futures Institute · deadline 02 Nov 2026 · Around seven commissions with budgets of GBP 8,000 to 12,000 each, inclusive of VAT and all costs. No application fee.
